summary: Iteration 7: Verified guest client-side cart feature end-to-end. Guest can add non-variant and variant products (variantSku captured) to localStorage key 'ar360_cart_v1'; header badge updates; cart-drawer CTA correctly reads 'Sign In or Register to Checkout' for guests, 'Become a Member to Checkout' for non-members (verified by registering a fresh user), and 'Proceed to Checkout' for members (confirmed in code + backend flow). CTA routes correctly to /auth, /membership, /checkout respectively. Quantity +/- and trash-remove update local state and persist to localStorage. Backend POST /api/orders now honours `items` array in body; variant pricing is correctly pulled from product.variants[*].price (not product.price). Empty items → 400, no auth → 401, non-member → 403. REGRESSION: /api/products returns 39, admin /admin-login -> /admin, /api/files image proxy returns 200, but Hampton Adams 2-Pack and Clinic Roll variant counts dropped from 10 → 5 (broken since iteration 6 snapshot).

critical.issue: Variant count regressed from 10 to 5. Iteration-6 baseline and this iteration's review request both require 10 variants per SKU. Current live data returns only 5 color variants (Black/Beige/Blue/Pink/Red) with no size variation.

critical_code_review_comments: cart-drawer.tsx subtotal uses item.product.price (base) instead of variant price when a variant is chosen. Guests see the wrong subtotal in the drawer if a variant's price differs from the base product price (backend computes the correct total at order time, but the UX mismatch can confuse users). Consider using variant.price when item.variantSku is set.

use-cart.tsx stores the entire Product snapshot (including potentially dozens of variants and long descriptions) in localStorage for every cart line. With a 5 MB localStorage quota this is fine today, but storing only {productId, variantSku, quantity} + a small display snapshot (name, imageUrl, unit price) would be leaner and avoid stale pricing being shown if product prices change while the cart sits idle.

orders.py line 131 sets new_order['_id'] = result.inserted_id then returns transform_order(new_order); transform_order correctly casts _id to string so no leak — but the in-memory dict is mutated in a way that makes it non-JSON-serialisable. Works due to transform_order but easy to break if someone returns new_order directly.

orders.py: when a productId in the submitted items array no longer exists or is malformed, the loop silently `continue`s. A client submitting only invalid items then hits the `not source_items` check only if the list starts empty — if the payload had one invalid entry, order creation will succeed with totalAmount=0 and items=[]. Recommend raising 400 if order_items is empty after processing.

checkout-form.tsx sends shippingAddress as a single concatenated string, dropping structured fields (city/state/zip). Downstream reporting/shipping integrations will have to re-parse this. Consider sending a structured shippingAddress object.

hcp_doctor_NOT_a_member.note: drsmith has isDoctor=true & hcpStatus=approved but isMember=false — cannot place orders without /api/membership/purchase.

seed_data_creation: Pytest fixture registers ephemeral TEST_member_<uuid> users and upgrades them via /api/membership/purchase. A few pending orders were created under these test users.

The auth note in /app/memory/test_credentials.md calls drsmith an 'HCP-approved member' but the DB has isMember=false — update the doc or re-seed drsmith with isMember=true to make member flows easier to smoke-test via UI.
rca_of_the_issue: Variant regression RCA (hypothesis): The iteration-6 catalog exported 10 Hampton Adams SKUs (likely 5 colors x 2 sizes/packs). A subsequent import or admin edit preserved only the 5 colors, dropping the second axis. Fix: re-run the Hampton Adams catalog import script or restore from the iteration-6 MongoDB snapshot, confirming that both products have hasVariants=true with 10 entries each and both attributes (color + size/pack) populated.
